html:
The Code noir was a decree of Louis XIV of March 1685 that set the rules of slavery in the French colonies. It was drafted with the planters of Martinique and Guadeloupe in mind.

It defined enslaved people as movable property. It required that they be baptised Catholic, banned work on Sundays, and set brutal punishments for running away, including branding and cutting off ears. In theory it also gave the enslaved some protections, which were rarely enforced.

It applied in Saint-Domingue, Louisiana and the Indian Ocean islands, and it stayed in force, with a break during the Revolution, until slavery was abolished in 1848 under Victor Schoelcher.
